newsitem.title: USA: Chicago budget unveiling set for Oct. 11.
newsitem.headline: Chicago budget unveiling set for Oct. 11.

text.p: Chicago Mayor Richard Daley plans to unveil a balanced budget on Oct. 11 that eliminates a projected $67.1 million shortfall, a city hall source said Tuesday.

The budget for the fiscal year that begins Jan. 1 may include some revenue increases, including a $9 million annual property tax hike to support a bond-financed, three-year $50 million capital program for libraries, the source said.
The budget is also expected to contain $150 million of bonds for general city improvements, the source added.

Chicago officials projected the $67.1 million shortfall in the preliminary $2 billion corporate fund budget last month as part of the city's normal budget preliminaries. Officials blamed the shortfall on wage increases for city employees and an approximately $20 million state-mandated increase in pension contributions by the city.
